components.css: .ds-field { background: var(--spruce, #173a30); padding: 32px; max-width: 464px; font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Schibsted Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-shape { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; } .ds-stock { fill: none; stroke: var(--lichen, #e4cb3a); stroke-opacity: 0.4; stroke-width: 2; stroke-dasharray: 4 8; } .ds-ink { fill: var(--lichen, #e4cb3a); } .ds-legend { list-style: none; margin: 24px 0 0; padding: 16px 0 0; border-top: 1px solid rgb(238 240 236 / 0.18); display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--on-spruce-soft, #b4c2bb); } .ds-legend li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-legend svg { fill: var(--on-spruce-soft, #b4c2bb); opacity: 0.6; } .ds-legend li.is-on { color: var(--lichen, #e4cb3a); font-weight: 600; } .ds-legend li.is-on svg { fill: var(--lichen, #e4cb3a); opacity: 1; }

narrative.overview:
Plainly is a 1960s–70s Finnish modernist poster inked in Espoo landscape colour. A deep spruce field owns one whole region of the shell and carries the brand, the intent shape and the intent sentence; the work happens on cool granite beside it. One bright ink, sulphur lichen, is reserved for the things that matter right now: the shape, the selected answer, what just changed. Everything else is ink on stone.

The world is flat ink. No gradients, no drop shadows, 2px corners, one 8px module for shape, type and layout. One display face appears at fixed steps, set bold and tight. Density is calm and operational: a question, a set of answer cells, a primary action, and a ledger of answers that restyles rows in place.

The signature is the intent shape: a single lichen polygon on spruce that starts out of focus and is cut, answer by answer, from a blunt stock toward one of three emblems, coming into sharp focus as the intent becomes plain. Motion is reserved for that moment; every other transition is a short state change.
keyCharacteristics: Total palette commitment: spruce field, granite ground, lichen as the only bright ink, rowan for errors only.
Flat ink, 2px corners, no shadows or gradients.
One 8px module (4px half-step) for spacing, shape geometry and type rhythm.
One display face (Familjen Grotesk 700) at fixed steps; Schibsted Grotesk for the interface.
One authored motion moment: the intent shape morph and focus pull (700ms, exponential ease-out).

rules.name: The One Bright Ink Rule
rules.body: Lichen marks the shape, the selection and the change, and nothing else. If an element is not one of those things, it is not lichen.

rules.name: The Rowan Is Alarm Rule
rules.body: Rowan appears only on error text. It never marks emphasis, a brand moment or a destructive-looking button.

rules.name: The Field Owns a Region Rule
rules.body: Spruce is applied as a whole region (the field, the primary button), never as a thin tint or a card background on granite.

rules.name: The Fixed Steps Rule
rules.body: Display type uses only the three named steps. No fluid clamp scaling; the steps change once, at the 900px breakpoint.

rules.name: The One Display Face Rule
rules.body: Familjen Grotesk is the only display face. Emphasis inside display type is colour (lichen on spruce), never italic: emphasis elements are set upright.

rules.name: The Flat Ink Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. State is shown by changing ink (background, border colour, border style), never by shadow or blur. Inset strokes that draw a line in solid ink are allowed; cast shadows are not. The single exception is the intent shape's focus blur, which carries meaning (how vague the intent still is) and reaches zero when the drill is complete.

rules.name: The Ring Follows the Ground Rule
rules.body: Focus is a 3px solid outline at 2px offset: spruce on granite surfaces, lichen on spruce surfaces. Every interactive element inside the field uses the lichen ring.

dos: Do keep lichen to the shape, selection, changed state and focus on spruce (The One Bright Ink Rule).
Do use the 2px radius and the 8px module (4px half-step) for every new component.
Do show state through ink: white fill and spruce border for chosen, dashed edges for empty, solid edges once filled.
Do switch the focus ring to lichen on any spruce surface, spruce on granite.
Do reserve height for status, error and intent text so nothing jumps.
Do draw icons as filled inline SVG on the 16-unit emblem grid.
Do write labels, empty states and errors as generic templates; put characterful language in question wording and static help text.
donts: Don't add drop shadows, glows, blur or gradients; depth is tonal only. The intent shape's focus blur is the one sanctioned blur (The Flat Ink Rule).
Don't use rowan for anything but errors.
Don't add a second display face, italic emphasis, or fluid display sizes between the fixed steps.
Don't add motion beyond short state transitions (120ms / 220ms); the shape morph is the one authored moment.
Don't write UI copy that reacts to the user's specific answers, or that explains what the product is not.
Don't present sample events or answers without a sample label, or show invented outcomes or match numbers.
